turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Good morning, everyone-just a quick heads-up before we dive in: Maya and Sam are out sick this week, so they'll be offline for any tickets or PR reviews.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Got it, thanks for the note, Daniel.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Yeah, hope they feel better soon.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Sure thing, I'll keep that in mind when I'm pairing later.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: Alright, noted.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Okay, moving on-since they're not here, any blockers that would have needed their input should be rerouted; if you need something from Maya or Sam, drop a Slack message and I'll try to cover or get them a quick sync when they're back.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Will do. Also, just to confirm, the sprint board still shows their tasks as 'in progress,' right?

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Exactly, the board reflects their current tickets as still in progress, but we’ll mark them as blocked if anything critical comes up, and I’ll make sure we don’t let any deadlines slip because of their absence.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: So the query planner rewrite is actually ahead of schedule; we hit the core planner unit tests yesterday and they all passed on the first run.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Nice, that’s good news.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Yeah, and the new cost-based optimizer is already showing a 12% reduction in average latency on our internal benchmark suite for the sales dashboard queries.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Impressive, did you pull the numbers from the latest 3.2-release data?

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Exactly, I ran it against the 3.2-release snapshot from Tuesday, same data set we use for the quarterly performance reports.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Cool, any gotchas we should know about?

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Actually, there is one surprise: the nested aggregation paths we thought would be a simple depth-first walk are triggering a stack overflow on queries that have more than seven levels of grouping, like the new multi-dimensional cohort analysis you’re working on.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: That sounds like a recursion limit issue.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Right, the planner builds a recursive CTE for each nested GROUP BY, and the Postgres planner stack defaults to 1000 frames, but our generated plan can exceed that when you have deep hierarchies, so it aborts with ERROR: stack depth limit exceeded.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Can we bump the limit?

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: We can, but it’s a temporary band-aid; the real fix is to refactor the planner to emit an iterative plan for deep nests, which will take another day or two to prototype.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Got it, so it’s not a blocker for the current sprint, just something to track.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Exactly, the current tickets are fine, but I’ll add a spike story for the iterative approach and we’ll prioritize it after the migration work is done.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Alright, so the events table migration is scheduled for tomorrow night, but I just hit a snag-our script needs a full DB lock for about 45 minutes, and we don’t have a maintenance window carved out yet.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Wait, we’re assuming a lock? I thought we were doing it online with logical replication?

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: We tried the online approach, but the bulk delete of old partitions triggers a cascade that blows up the transaction log; the only safe path right now is the offline lock.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: Yeah, the backfill job we ran last week showed the same pattern-once you hit more than 10 M rows the write-ahead log stalls.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Exactly, and the script also does a column type change on the event_payload JSONB, which requires a rewrite of the whole table. That rewrite can’t happen while the table is serving traffic, otherwise we get deadlocks with the real-time ingestion workers.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: So are we looking at a full outage? How long would that be, roughly?

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Based on the dry-run on staging, about 42 minutes total-30 minutes for the rewrite, plus 12 minutes for the index rebuild and validation. We’d need to coordinate with support to put the API gateway into read-only mode during that window.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Alright, I’ll take ownership of scheduling that window. I’ll ping support and see if we can slip it in between the 2 am and 3 am maintenance slot on Thursday, since we have a low traffic window then.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Sounds good. I’ll drop the updated migration plan into the #infra-ops channel, and I’ll add a note about the lock requirement so nobody starts the ingestion pipeline during that period.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: What if we spin up a shadow table and sync changes via logical decoding? Could that avoid the full lock?

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: We tried that last sprint for the user_events table, but the volume of updates blew the replication slot; the lag grew to 15 minutes and we’d still have to cut over, which defeats the purpose.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Also, the nested aggregation work means the planner will be hitting the same rewrite path; adding a shadow copy just doubles the I/O.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: But the UI team can tolerate a brief read-only mode, right? If we can keep ingestion alive and just block reads, maybe that's acceptable.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Read-only mode still requires us to pause the API gateway; that’s effectively an outage for our clients, even if the backend keeps writing.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: What about using pg_repack to do an online rebuild? It can rewrite the table in chunks without a full lock.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: pg_repack works for simple column adds, but we need to change the JSONB column type and drop old partitions; pg_repack can’t handle that cascade safely, it would still need a brief exclusive lock at the end.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: So the only way to stay fully online is to break the migration into multiple smaller steps, but that adds complexity and risk.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Exactly, and with the sprint deadline looming, the safest path is the offline lock we discussed, then we can revisit an online strategy for the next iteration.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: Guys, I just got the latest cost report from CloudWatch and we're seeing a $12,500 jump this week compared to the baseline.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Whoa, that's a big spike. Any idea what's driving it?

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: Yes, it traces back to the backfill job we kicked off on March 12th for the historic events; it's been running nonstop and pulling about 850 GB of data per hour.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Is that the same job that was supposed to finish in three days?

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: Exactly, but because of the new JSONB schema change we added, the job's query planner kept re-optimizing and ended up doing a full table scan on every batch, which blew up both CPU and I/O.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: I saw the CPU usage hit 95% on the primary replica yesterday, but I thought the backfill was throttled?

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: We set a throttle, but the logical replication slot kept falling behind, so the system auto-scaled the read replicas, and each scale-up added roughly $1,200 per hour in instance costs.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: So the cost spike is essentially the side effect of the backfill not being rate-limited properly and the auto-scaling kicking in?

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: That's right. If we pause the backfill now and re-run it with a tighter batch size-say 5 million rows per chunk-and enforce a max of two extra replicas, we should bring the weekly spend back under $3,000.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Alright, I'll have the ops team put a hold on the backfill and adjust the scaling policies. Thanks for catching that, Chris.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Okay, quick update on the cohort builder-performance is still lagging behind the SLA we promised to Fielder last month.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Right, the Fielder team flagged that the latency hit 12 seconds on the UI, they’re not happy.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: We dug into the logs and found the main culprit is the new aggregation layer we added for dynamic segment filters; it’s doing a full scan on the users table for each filter combo.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Is that the same code path that the query planner rewrite touched?

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Exactly, Yuki. The planner thinks it can push down the predicates, but because of the JSONB payload size, the planner picks a sequential scan instead of the index we built on the tenant_id column.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: So we’re basically re-processing millions of rows per request?

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Yes, and on top of that the cache warm-up isn’t happening because the cache key includes the full filter JSON, which is unique per request, so we never hit a hit.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: My proposal: we add a materialized view that pre-aggregates the most common filter combos-Fielder’s top three use cases cover about 70% of traffic-and we rewrite the builder to fall back to that view when the filter matches, otherwise we fall back to the current path but with a hard timeout of 5 seconds.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Sounds like a plan. Let's get a ticket in for the view and have Yuki scope the rewrite. We'll update Fielder by EOD.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Alright, folks, we have a separate blocker on the events table migration that we need to nail down today.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Right, the script needs a maintenance window, but we haven't booked anything yet.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Exactly. I'm going to take ownership of that and coordinate with the support team to lock down a slot.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Do we have any constraints on when the window can be? Our rewrite is still in QA, but we don't want to clash with the nightly batch.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: The migration touches the events partitioning, so we need to run it when the write traffic is at its lowest-ideally between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC on a weekday. That way we avoid the 3 am US-East batch and the 4 am EU sync.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: That window works for me, but we should also confirm the replica lag is under 5 seconds before we start.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: I'll set up a quick call with the ops lead, Maya-oh wait, Maya's out sick this week-so I'll loop in Sam instead, get his sign-off on the downtime, and then raise a Change Request in ServiceNow with the exact time window, the rollback plan, and the monitoring steps.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: Make sure to tag the cost-impact note we discussed, otherwise finance will ping us again.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Will do, Chris. I'll also add a note that the migration script has been tested on the staging cluster up to 10 million rows, and we'll do a dry-run at 01:30 UTC just to verify everything before the actual cutover.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Sounds good. Let us know once the window is confirmed so we can adjust any dependent jobs.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Will update the channel by EOD. Thanks, everyone.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Before we wrap, just a quick heads-up: we're shifting the on-call rotation forward by one week starting next Monday so Sam will cover the first night of the migration window.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Got it, so my Friday night shift moves to next Thursday? I need to update my calendar.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Yeah, I saw the Slack note-my Saturday slot is now Friday night, which actually works better for me.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Just to confirm, does that mean the handoff meeting moves too, or are we keeping the 9 am sync?

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: We keep the 9 am sync, but the primary on-call will be whoever is on the new schedule, so the escalation path changes accordingly.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Exactly-so the rotation list in the Confluence page gets a one-row bump, and I've already pinged support leads; they'll adjust the alert routing in PagerDuty. If anyone sees a mismatch, raise it now.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: Will do. I'll double-check the alert policies after the change; I don't want any false positives during the migration dry-run at 01:30 UTC.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: Sounds solid. Thanks for the quick update, Daniel.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Alright, that's everything for today-thanks for the updates, everyone.

turns.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
turns.text: One quick thing-just confirming my next sprint focus is still the nested aggregation edge cases, right?

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Yep, Yuki, keep that on track; we’ll sync after the migration when the new planner is live.

turns.speaker: Tom Bradley
turns.text: And I’ll keep an eye on the replica lag during the dry-run, will post metrics in the channel.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Perfect, Tom. And if you hit anything unexpected, shout immediately; we have the ops lead on standby.

turns.speaker: Rachel Goldstein
turns.text: Got it. I'll make sure the cohort builder tests run after the window, so we can validate the Fielder fix.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Thanks, Rachel-just tag the test run with #migration-validation so we can filter later.

turns.speaker: Chris Lindqvist
turns.text: I'll monitor the cost spike on the backfill and update the ticket if it exceeds the threshold we set.

turns.speaker: Daniel Okonkwo
turns.text: Appreciate it, Chris. If anything else comes up before the 01:30 UTC dry-run, drop a note here. Otherwise, see you all tomorrow at 9 am. Have a good one!
